underTheHoodPage.metaDescription: Узнайте, как DashBeam обеспечивает прямую peer-to-peer передачу файлов с билетами, iroh, шифрованием QUIC, NAT traversal, сопряжением устройств и open-source релеями, без аккаунтов и IP-адресов.
underTheHoodPage.title: Под капотом
underTheHoodPage.intro: Это как scp без необходимости знать IP-адрес. Добавьте файлы в DashBeam, и он выдаст вставляемый билет, который можно передать любому, кому нужны ваши файлы. DashBeam напрямую соединит устройства и передаст данные без аккаунтов и настройки.

concepts.peerDiscovery: Обнаружение пиров, hole punching и NAT traversal

blobs.title: Blobs
blobs.intro: Контент-адресуемое хранение и передача blob. iroh-blobs реализует request/response и потоковую передачу blob произвольного размера с BLAKE3-проверенными потоками и контент-адресуемыми ссылками.

items.blob: Blob: непрозрачная последовательность байтов (без встроенных метаданных).
items.hashSeq: HashSeq: blob, содержащий последовательность ссылок (полезно для chunking/деревьев).
items.provider: Provider / Requester: provider отдаёт данные; requester их получает. Endpoint может быть и тем, и другим.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.body: Билеты - способ делиться информацией для подключения между iroh endpoints. Это один токен со всем необходимым для подключения к другому endpoint или получения blob. Содержит Ed25519 NodeIds: криптографическую идентичность вашего устройства. Эта схема значительно лучше full P2P-систем, транслирующих ваш IP. В iroh билеты формируют «cozy network» между пирами, с которыми вы явно хотите соединиться. Можно перейти в «full p2p» и транслировать детали подключения, но билеты - лучший компромисс по умолчанию.

peerDiscovery.title: Обнаружение пиров, NAT Traversal и Hole Punching
peerDiscovery.body: Пиры регистрируются при запуске на open-source публичных relay-серверах для обхода firewall и NAT. После подключения iroh использует QUIC hole punching для прямого P2P-соединения, обходя relay. При возможности прямого соединения общение идёт напрямую с E2E-шифрованием; иначе relay временно служит fallback. Это обеспечивает надёжные соединения в локальной сети и через интернет.

quic.title: QUIC и шифрование
quic.intro: QUIC - современный транспортный протокол на UDP, снижающий задержку и улучшающий веб-производительность по сравнению с TCP. Изначально Google, стандартизирован IETF как основа HTTP/3, интегрирует TLS 1.3 прямо в протокол.

powers.zeroRtt: установка соединения с нулевым RTT, если вы уже подключались к endpoint

relays.title: Релеи
relays.body: DashBeam использует open-source публичные relay-серверы для прямых соединений, ускорения первоначального подключения и fallback при неудаче. Все соединения E2E-зашифрованы. Relay - «ещё один UDP-сокет» для зашифрованных пакетов. <link>Читать далее</link>.

pairing.title: Сопряжение и управляющий канал
pairing.intro: Билеты работают с кем угодно, но между собственными устройствами копировать их вручную быстро надоедает. Сопряжение позволяет двум устройствам запомнить друг друга и обмениваться билетами по второму, выделенному каналу — отдельному протоколу на той же конечной точке iroh, отделённому от пути передачи блобов.

items.pairingCode: Код сопряжения: хост открывает короткое окно сопряжения и показывает код, который представляет собой просто его идентификатор конечной точки — в виде QR-кода или строки для вставки. Ничего другого вне соединения не передаётся; подсказка о релее прилагается, только если хост использует собственное реле.
items.closed: По умолчанию закрыт: вне этого окна управляющий канал отклоняет подключения любого устройства, с которым вы не сопряжены, ещё до чтения первого сообщения.
items.proof: Взаимное подтверждение: каждая сторона подписывает ключевой материал, экспортированный из живого QUIC-соединения, своим ключом устройства Ed25519 и проверяет подпись собеседника по его идентификатору конечной точки. Подпись привязана именно к этому соединению, поэтому её нельзя воспроизвести в другом.
items.consent: Согласие с обеих сторон: пара сохраняется, только если оба устройства согласились запомнить друг друга. Любая сторона может позже её забыть — запрос на удаление подписывается и доставляется, поэтому действует на обоих устройствах.
items.presence: Присутствие вместо опроса: сопряжённые устройства держат управляющее соединение открытым и заново подтверждают личность при каждом переподключении. Статус «в сети / не в сети» определяется тем, живо ли это соединение; после обрыва попытки повторяются с растущей паузой.
items.invites: Приглашения, а не обходные пути: при отправке на сопряжённое устройство по-прежнему создаётся обычный одноразовый блоб-билет. Управляющий канал лишь доставляет его как приглашение внутри приложения, которое получатель принимает или отклоняет. Сама передача идёт тем же путём, что и по вставленному билету.

faq.title: Часто задаваемые вопросы

faq1.question: What is DashBeam and how does it work?
faq1.answer: DashBeam is an open-source peer-to-peer file transfer app for desktop, Android, web, and CLI. It lets you send files and folders anywhere in the world with no accounts and no cloud storage. It is built on the <link>Iroh networking stack</link> and uses ticket-based sharing with NAT hole punching and encrypted relay fallback.

faq2.question: Is DashBeam free to use?
faq2.answer: Yes. DashBeam is free and open source (AGPL-3.0) with no file size limits, no upload quotas, and no accounts. If you benefit from this work, consider supporting development through Buy Me a Coffee or GitHub Sponsors.

faq3.question: What file types can I transfer with DashBeam?
faq3.answer: You can transfer anything: images, videos, documents, folders, and more. Integrity checks use BLAKE3 on both ends, so files are verified during send and receive. Transfers are resumable if interrupted.

faq4.question: How secure is my data when using DashBeam?
faq4.answer: DashBeam uses end-to-end encryption with QUIC + TLS 1.3. Files go directly between devices and are not stored on a cloud server. Relays only see encrypted traffic. Tickets authenticate the intended sender before a transfer starts.

faq5.question: How does DashBeam compare to FilePizza, Wormhole, and PairDrop?
faq5.answer: Unlike browser-only WebRTC tools, DashBeam is a native app (plus Android, web, and CLI) built on Iroh/QUIC. You can send large files and full folders with pause/resume, fewer browser limits, and BLAKE3-verified streaming. See our <compareLink>full comparison</compareLink> for details.

faq6.question: Do I need an internet connection to use DashBeam?
faq6.answer: A network connection is required so devices can reach each other. On the same LAN/Wi-Fi, full internet is not required. Across different networks, internet is used for hole punching or encrypted relay fallback, so DashBeam works over the internet, not only on local Wi-Fi.

faq7.question: Is DashBeam a LocalSend alternative for the internet?
faq7.answer: Yes. LocalSend is excellent for nearby devices on the same local network. DashBeam is built for the same frictionless feel across any network, local or across the internet, using Iroh tickets, QUIC encryption, and optional relays. Compare them on our <compareLink>LocalSend comparison page</compareLink>.

faq8.question: Is DashBeam an open-source Blip (blip.net) alternative?
faq8.answer: Yes. DashBeam is a free, open-source alternative to Blip (blip.net): unlimited file size, no accounts, end-to-end encrypted peer-to-peer transfers, and apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and the web. See <compareLink>DashBeam vs Blip</compareLink>.

faq9.question: Является ли DashBeam тем же, что AltSendme / Alt Send Me / alt-sendme?
faq9.answer: Да. DashBeam является новым именем AltSendme (также известного как Alt Send Me, alt-sendme и Altsendme). Это тот же проект с открытым исходным кодом, тот же репозиторий GitHub и тот же продукт для одноранговой передачи файлов.

localsend.metaDescription: DashBeam is a LocalSend alternative that works over the internet, not just the same Wi-Fi. Open-source P2P with Iroh gigabit speeds, tickets, Android, web, and CLI.
localsend.title: LocalSend alternative for the internet
localsend.lead: LocalSend is excellent for nearby devices on the same network. DashBeam keeps that frictionless feel across the internet, and adds Iroh/QUIC networking that can saturate gigabit links, plus a real CLI compatible with sendme.
localsend.whenLocalsend1: Both devices are on the same Wi-Fi or LAN
localsend.whenLocalsend2: You want automatic nearby device discovery
localsend.whenLocalsend3: You do not need internet-wide transfers
localsend.whenAltsendme1: Devices are on different networks or across the internet
localsend.whenAltsendme2: You want ticket-based sharing and Iroh speeds that can fill a gigabit pipe
localsend.whenAltsendme3: You need CLI/sendme interop, resumable large folders, or a web app
localsend.faq1q: Does LocalSend work over the internet?
localsend.faq1a: No. LocalSend is built for the same local network. It discovers nearby devices on your Wi-Fi or LAN and transfers directly between them. It does not support sending files to someone on a different network or across the internet. DashBeam fills that gap with Iroh tickets, NAT hole punching, and encrypted relays so peers can connect locally or worldwide.
localsend.faq2a: Not yet. Resumable transfers are a long-standing LocalSend feature request but remain unshipped. If Wi-Fi drops or a transfer is interrupted, you start over from the beginning. DashBeam supports resumable transfers: large files and folders pick up where they left off, with BLAKE3 integrity verification on both ends.
localsend.faq3q: Is DashBeam open source like LocalSend?
localsend.faq3a: Yes. Both apps are free and open source with no accounts or upload limits. DashBeam is AGPL-3.0 and built on the Iroh networking stack; LocalSend is MIT-licensed. You can audit either codebase and run transfers without vendor lock-in.
localsend.faq4a: LocalSend scans your local network and lists nearby devices automatically, ideal when everyone shares the same Wi-Fi. DashBeam uses shareable Iroh tickets: one peer generates a ticket, the other pastes or scans it. That works on the same LAN and across the internet, without relying on broadcast discovery.
localsend.faq5a: Yes. DashBeam interoperates with the official Iroh sendme CLI. Tickets work across the GUI and terminal for scripting and automation. LocalSend offers desktop and mobile apps but no CLI or browser client. DashBeam also includes a web app alongside Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
localsend.faq6q: Which is better for large folders?
localsend.faq6a: For multi-gigabyte folders on an unreliable connection, resumability matters. LocalSend does not resume failed transfers, so a drop near the end means re-sending everything. DashBeam streams folders with pause and resume, can saturate gigabit links on native apps via QUIC, and verifies integrity with BLAKE3, better suited for big payloads that may not finish in one session.

blip.metaDescription: DashBeam is a free, open-source alternative to Blip (blip.net). Unlimited P2P with CLI, Iroh gigabit speeds, no accounts, and apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and web.
blip.title: Open-source Blip (blip.net) alternative
blip.lead: Blip (blip.net) is a popular proprietary large-file transfer app. DashBeam is the open-source alternative: unlimited size, no accounts, a real CLI, end-to-end encrypted P2P on Iroh that can saturate gigabit connections, and full transparency under AGPL-3.0.
blip.whenBlip1: You already rely on Blip’s proprietary workflow
blip.whenBlip2: You prefer a closed commercial product
blip.whenAltsendme1: You want open source you can audit and self-host relays for
blip.whenAltsendme2: You need free unlimited transfers, CLI/sendme interop, and no account lock-in
blip.whenAltsendme3: You want Iroh networking that can push multi-gigabit on a good path
blip.faq1q: Is there a free open-source Blip (blip.net) alternative?
blip.faq1a: Yes. DashBeam is a free, open-source alternative to Blip (blip.net), with unlimited peer-to-peer transfers, CLI support, and no cloud storage of your files.
blip.faq2a: No. Drop a file, share a ticket, and transfer directly, with no signup. Use the GUI or the sendme-compatible CLI.
blip.faq3a: Yes. Transfers use QUIC + TLS 1.3 on Iroh. Relays only forward encrypted packets, and native transfers can saturate gigabit links.

wormhole.metaTitle: Magic Wormhole Alternative with GUI & Resumable Transfers
wormhole.metaDescription: DashBeam is a Magic Wormhole alternative with native GUI apps, Android, web, and sendme CLI, plus Iroh/QUIC gigabit speeds and resumable folders.
wormhole.title: Magic Wormhole alternative with a full GUI
wormhole.lead: Magic Wormhole pioneered secure CLI file sharing with memorable short codes. DashBeam shares the same values: open source, no accounts, end-to-end encryption, but ships official GUI apps for desktop, Android, and web, with resumable folders and Iroh/QUIC networking that can saturate gigabit links.
wormhole.whenWormhole1: You live in the terminal and love the wormhole-send workflow
wormhole.whenWormhole2: Short human-readable codes via a mailbox relay are exactly what you need
wormhole.whenWormhole3: You send occasional one-off files and do not need a GUI or resume
wormhole.whenAltsendme1: You want native GUI apps on desktop, Android, and web, not CLI only
wormhole.whenAltsendme2: You need resumable large-folder transfers that survive dropped connections
wormhole.whenAltsendme3: You want Iroh/QUIC tickets that work across the GUI and sendme CLI
wormhole.faq1q: Is DashBeam the same as Magic Wormhole?
wormhole.faq1a: No. They are different projects on different protocols. Magic Wormhole uses PAKE-secured encrypted TCP with short codes delivered through a relay mailbox. DashBeam is built on Iroh/QUIC with ticket-based sharing and the sendme CLI. Both are open source, end-to-end encrypted, and avoid cloud file storage, but tickets and wormhole codes are not interchangeable.
wormhole.faq2q: Does Magic Wormhole have an official GUI?
wormhole.faq2a: The core Magic Wormhole project is CLI-only (wormhole send). Community GUI frontends exist but are separately maintained and can lag behind the CLI. DashBeam ships official apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and a web client, all sharing tickets with the sendme CLI.
wormhole.faq3q: How do wormhole codes compare to Iroh tickets?
wormhole.faq3a: Wormhole gives you a short code through a mailbox relay: the receiver types it in. DashBeam uses Iroh tickets: longer strings you paste or scan, encoding connection details for QUIC hole punching and relay fallback. Both avoid accounts. Tickets are better suited to streaming large folders with resume on Iroh.
wormhole.faq4q: Can Magic Wormhole resume interrupted transfers?
wormhole.faq4a: No. If a wormhole transfer fails partway through, you start over. DashBeam supports resumable transfers with BLAKE3 integrity checks on both ends, important for multi-gigabyte folders on flaky Wi-Fi or long internet paths.
wormhole.faq5q: Which is faster for large files?
wormhole.faq5a: Wormhole can be fast on a direct TCP path between reachable peers. DashBeam uses QUIC over Iroh and can saturate gigabit links on native desktop and mobile apps. Iroh's hole punching establishes direct QUIC connections in most cases, with encrypted relays as fallback.
wormhole.faq6q: Are both open source and free?
wormhole.faq6a: Yes. Magic Wormhole is MIT-licensed; DashBeam is AGPL-3.0. Neither requires accounts or charges for transfers. You can audit either codebase and run transfers without vendor lock-in.

pairdrop.metaTitle: PairDrop Alternative with Native Apps & Resumable Folders
pairdrop.metaDescription: DashBeam is a PairDrop alternative with native desktop and Android apps, resumable folders, no browser memory ceiling, and gigabit Iroh/QUIC speeds.
pairdrop.title: PairDrop alternative without browser limits
pairdrop.lead: PairDrop makes quick browser-based sharing effortless, especially on the same Wi-Fi. DashBeam targets the same frictionless feel as native apps on Iroh/QUIC: resumable folders, no in-browser memory ceiling, gigabit-class throughput, and tickets that work across GUI, web, and sendme CLI.
pairdrop.whenPairdrop1: You want zero install: just open a browser tab and send
pairdrop.whenPairdrop2: Files are small to medium and WebRTC speed limits are acceptable
pairdrop.whenPairdrop3: Everyone is on the same LAN and nearby discovery is enough
pairdrop.whenAltsendme1: You are moving large files or full folders that may not finish in one session
pairdrop.whenAltsendme2: You need resumability and throughput beyond WebRTC/SCTP browser ceilings
pairdrop.whenAltsendme3: You want desktop, Android, web, and sendme CLI sharing the same tickets
pairdrop.faq1q: How is DashBeam different from PairDrop?
pairdrop.faq1a: PairDrop runs in the browser over WebRTC, great for quick shares, but capped by SCTP throughput and in-memory file handling. DashBeam is a native app on Iroh/QUIC with resumable folders, no browser RAM ceiling, gigabit-capable transfers on desktop and mobile, and sendme CLI interop.
pairdrop.faq2q: Does PairDrop work over the internet?
pairdrop.faq2a: PairDrop can connect across the internet via WebRTC ICE/STUN, but throughput and file size are limited by the browser stack. DashBeam uses Iroh tickets, QUIC hole punching, and encrypted relays, built for large internet transfers without loading the entire file into browser memory.
pairdrop.faq3a: The browser PWA focuses on individual files; reliable folder sending often depends on the CLI fork or workarounds. DashBeam sends full folders natively in the GUI and CLI, with pause and resume if the connection drops.
pairdrop.faq4q: Why are browser transfers slower than native apps?
pairdrop.faq4a: WebRTC data channels use SCTP inside the browser, which rarely saturates a fast connection and buffers file data in memory. DashBeam streams directly over QUIC with native disk I/O, better for multi-gigabyte payloads on gigabit links.
pairdrop.faq5q: Do I need to install DashBeam?
pairdrop.faq5a: PairDrop's main advantage is no install: open a tab and go. DashBeam offers a web client, but the best experience is the native desktop or Android app: resumable transfers, unlimited practical file size, CLI automation, and much higher throughput than a browser tab.
pairdrop.faq6a: Yes. PairDrop is GPL-3.0; DashBeam is AGPL-3.0. Neither requires accounts. DashBeam adds auditable Iroh networking with self-hostable relays if you want full control over the infrastructure.
